Q: Why do you not explicitly call finalize() or start the garbage collector? A:

This reply is to provide some updates reflecting "recent" Java changes (as of 2026).

It remains a fact that calling System.gc() is bad for efficiency1.

The previously mentioned advice to "use the concurrent mark/sweep" collector is no longer correct. The CMS collector was superseded by the G1 collector (in Java 9) and was removed in Java 14. There are a couple of other alternatives: Z and Shenandoah2. The Java documentation gives advice on selecting the GC here:

  • HotSpot Virtual Machine Garbage Collection Tuning Guide in the "Selecting a Collector" section.

Finalizers have been deprecated for removal since Java 9, and "deprecated for removal" since Java 18. That alone is a good reason not to use them. JEP 421: Deprecate Finalization for Removal includes material on the motivation for the removal.

Alternatives to finalizers are try-with-resources (since Java 7) and the Cleaner API introduced in Java 9.

It is worth noting that the Cleaner API uses PhantomReference and ReferenceQueue under the hood. Like finalizers, cleaners have an impact on overall GC performance. You should be cautious about using them to implement (for example) object pooling.

Other answers have explained why calling finalize() is conceptually wrong ... even in cases where it is harmless from a purely technical standpoint.

1 - In nearly all cases, the JVM knows the best time to start a garbage collection. Triggering the GC at the wrong time will typically result in sub-optimal "GC cost per byte reclaimed" (i.e. wasted CPU) and/or unnecessary pauses. The only technically sound reasons for manually triggering the GC in production code are to (try to) avoid small CMS / G1 / Z collector pauses at inopportune moments; e.g. in a highly interactive game, you might trigger a GC on (say) switching levels ... when the user is going to be tolerant of a GC pause.

2 - The Shenandoah collector (maintained by Redhat) is not available in some OpenJDK distros. In others it is an "experimental" feature. You can check using java -XX:+UseShenandoahGC -version. Shenandoah's generational mode was added as "experimental" in Java 24; see JEP 521: Generational Shenandoah.

Q: How to fix executor failed running [/bin/sh -c pip install --upgrade --force-reinstall pip==9.0.3 && pip install --upgrade 'setuptools<45']: A:

I had the same issue, the problem was the base image I was using. Once I changed it to a working one the error disappeared. I specifically used a python3.9.10-slim image from our local repo. Once I switched to the regular python3.9.0 image all worked well.

The python3.9.10-slim image being corrupted is a problem in our repo but maybe what you're experiencing is caused by the same type of issue.

Q: how to fix groovy.lang.MissingMethodException: No signature of method: java.util.ArrayList.get() is applicable for argument types: () values: [] A:

If you want the list to be assigned to groupedDocs, Remove the .get() from the below line

groupedDocs = reader.selectGroupedDocs(last_update_date.toString()).get();

The get method in the list expects an argument. If you are trying to assign a particular value in the list to groupedDocs you need to pass in an index in the get method in order to retrieve it.

Eg. groupedDocs = reader.selectGroupedDocs(last_update_date.toString()).get(1);

Q: Weblogic Ant JWSC task to generate a webservice war file A:

I'm betting that in your deployment target (Which isn't posted here) is trying to 'clean' up the deployment directory, and is failing when it can't find the file called /var/tmp/_927vxb/web.xml

3 suggestions:

  1. Run touch /var/tmp/_927vxb/web.xml from the command line and try to run the build/deployment again. This will create an empty file that will at least let you get past the file not found on delete error. This is not a long term solution, but rather an attempt to expose the real issue.

  2. Look at line 231 in your /wls_domains/CIT/cruisecontrol-bin-2.8.3/util/Ivy/build.xml file. Perhaps there is a delete ant task that is failing on error. If this is the case, add `failonerror="false" to the ant task that is causing the issue.

  3. Post more of your build file here. Being able to align the line numbers in the file with the error will help in decoding the issue.

Q: How to override the DCB attributes in SFTP with phpseclib A: 
sftp> ls /+mode=text,lrecl=80,recfm=fb

The above is OpenSSH sftp client command ls. Internally, it issues a sequence of SFTP requests (OPENDIR, READDIR, CLOSE) to retrieve a directory listing.

The SFTP server is implemented to treat OPENDIR with that unique syntax specifically, as documented in the article you link to.

echo $sftp->exec('ls /+mode=text,lrecl=80,recfm=fb');

While the above executes a remote shell ls command. The shell ls command does not have a special treatment for the syntax and considers it a path and fails.

Note that while you execute the exec on $sftp instance, the method is actually implemented in parent SSH2 class and has nothing to do with SFTP.

To emulate the ls command of OpenSSH sftp (i.e. to send OPENDIR SFTP request), use some of the directory listing commands of SFTP class, like nlist or rawlist:

$sftp->nlist('/+mode=text,lrecl=80,recfm=fb');
